title: DeepInfer column: the other end of inference
deck: Strata runs a large model on one machine. DeepSeek's DeepInfer lets hundreds of GPUs serve a huge number of users together. The same ideas, done on a cluster.

pages.title: The other end: how DeepSeek runs inference on a cluster
pages.deck: What DeepInfer is, which part was open-sourced, what parts the production system is made of, and how it differs from Strata.

pages.title: Wide expert parallelism: spreading experts across 64 GPUs
pages.deck: Attention uses data parallelism. Experts use expert parallelism over 64–128 GPUs, so each GPU reads fewer experts per step. Then EPLB copies popular experts to even out the busiest GPU.

pages.title: E/P/D disaggregation and the 72-hour KV cache
pages.deck: The vision encoder, prefill and decode are deployed separately. The KV cache goes into a dedicated 3FS cluster and is read back on a hit. If SWA is missing, only the last short stretch of tokens is replayed.

pages.title: DSpark speculative decoding and zero-overhead scheduling
pages.deck: Drafts guess 5 tokens at once, confidence decides how many to verify, and the CPU prepares the next batch one step ahead so the GPU never stops.

pages.title: Batch invariance, deterministic sampling and structured outputs
pages.deck: Put the same request next to different batch neighbors, and the order of a floating-point sum can change. DeepInfer pins down both the summation order and the random numbers, then uses a bitmask so the model emits only a legal format.

title: DeepSeek column: the same model, one computer
deck: Strata uses another engine, strata-dsv41, to run DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one computer: the experts sit in three tiers, the lookup table sits on the SSD, and the draft model and conversation parking add speed together.

pages.title: The same model, on one computer
pages.deck: A cluster splits DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash across dozens of cards. One computer can only fit it in tiers across VRAM, RAM and the SSD. Every placement, measured speed and quality number on this page carries its measurement conditions.

pages.title: Where 288 GB of experts live
pages.deck: Three tiers hold the experts: VRAM, slots in RAM and direct reads from the SSD. A hot-expert profile and prefetch cut the waiting. The Faster mode uses one expert fewer per token.

pages.title: The 128-row window, compressed rows and the indexer
pages.deck: Each token reads only the latest 128 rows plus at most 512 picked compressed rows; the indexer picks the rows, and the window ring and compressed rows decide what state a token leaves behind.

pages.title: Engram: a big table that lives on the SSD
pages.deck: A hash table of about 768 million rows: each token yields 48 row numbers, the rows are read from the SSD, pass through a gate and are added back to the state. The hard part is latency, not bandwidth.

pages.title: DSpark drafts, the verify window and conversation parking
pages.deck: The draft model guesses 5 tokens at a time, and two confidence gates trim the verify window. Conversation state is parked in RAM and on disk, and the serving layer translates thinking effort and tool calls.
